department: School of Engineering and Engineering Technology

deadline.value: Graduate engineering applications are rolling, but applicants should submit all required materials by the Fall priority deadline of March 31 (March 31, 2027 inferred for Fall 2027; Spring is September 30; Summer not offered).
deadline.quote: Graduate program applications are accepted on a rolling basis. However, for full consideration, applicants are strongly encouraged to submit all required materials by the priority deadlines below: – Fall Admission: March 31 – Spring Admission: September 30 Please note that summer admission is not offered.

also.quote: Application Deadlines: March 31st for fall admission. September 30th for spring admissions. Summer admissions are not offered.

gre_general.value: GRE General Test is required (315 V+Q combined and 3.5 AW expected); catalog text lists waivers for UA Little Rock M.S. ECE thesis graduates (>=3.5 GPA), exceptional cases, or where GRE is unavailable in the applicant's country.
gre_general.quote: Applicants are required to submit GRE scores with the admission application. A combined total of 315 on the verbal and quantitative reasoning sections and a score of 3.5 on the analytical writing section will be expected. The GRE may be waived for applicants who graduate from UA Little Rock with a master’s degree in electrical and computer engineering (thesis option) and a 3.5 GPA or higher.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for Mechanical Engineering (ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Applicants are encouraged to contact engineering faculty for research supervision; advisor availability and willingness are considered in admission decisions (students formally declare an advisor by the end of the 2nd semester).
supervisor.quote: Applicants are encouraged to contact engineering faculty for their research supervision. The availability and willingness of advisors will be considered in making admission decisions.

funding.value: A limited number of competitive TAs/RAs are available to qualified full-time students with regular admission, covering 9 credits of tuition per semester plus a living stipend (university minimum $15,000/9-mo from Fall 2026) and $400/semester health insurance reimbursement.
funding.quote: A limited number of graduate assistantships that support teaching and research opportunities are available to qualified full-time students with regular admissions. Tuition is paid for nine credits per semester, and a stipend is provided for living expenses.

also.quote: The full-time stipend for the academic year is a minimum of $15,000 for doctoral students and $10,000 for master’s students.
The Doctoral Health Insurance Reimbursement provides $400 of insurance reimbursement for Fall and another $400 for Spring.

entry_route.value: Requires at least one degree (bachelor's or master's) in engineering: >=3.5 undergraduate GPA for bachelor's entry (72 credit hours) or >=3.3–3.5 master's GPA for master's entry (48 credit hours; department page states 3.3 while 2026-2027 catalog states 3.5).
entry_route.quote: Applicants must have at least one degree (bachelor’s or master’s) in engineering. Applicants with only a bachelor’s degree in engineering must have an overall undergraduate GPA of 3.5 or better. Applicants with a master’s degree in engineering should have a master’s GPA of 3.5 or better. | 72 hours for students entering the PhD program with a Bachelor’s degree and 48 hours for students entering the Ph.D. program with a Master’s degree.

also.quote: Alternatively, applicants with a master’s degree in engineering should have a master’s GPA of 3.3 or better.
